message.content:
**The Three Great Schisms in Christian History** | # | Schism | Approximate Dates | Key Causes & Outcomes | |---|--------|-------------------|-----------------------| | **1** | **Great Schism (East–West Schism)** | 1054 CE | • Doctrinal differences (e.g., Filioque clause, papal primacy).
• Cultural & political tensions between Latin West and Greek East.
• Resulted in the permanent split between the Roman Catholic Church (Western) and the Eastern Orthodox Churches. | | **2** | **Protestant Reformation** | 1517–1648 CE | • Initiated by Martin Luther’s 95 Theses (1517).
• Spread through Europe via translation of the Bible, printing press, and political alliances.
• Led to the formation of numerous Protestant denominations (Lutheran, Calvinist, Anglican, Anabaptist, etc.) and the Counter‑Reformation within Catholicism. | | **3** | **East–West Schism (Second Great Schism)** | 1965 CE | • Formalized the separation between the **Catholic Church** and the **Church of England** (Anglican Communion).
• Rooted in theological disputes (e.g., authority of the Pope, liturgical practices) and political factors (English Reformation under Henry VIII).
• Established the Anglican Communion as a distinct tradition while maintaining ties with the wider Protestant world. | These three events represent the most significant and lasting divisions in Christian history, each reshaping theology, ecclesiology, and the political landscape of Christendom.
